claims.claim_vi: Encoding (e.g. Base64) changes the format by a reversible scheme without a key and is not meant to secure data; encryption uses an algorithm and a key so only holders of the key can read the data; tokenization substitutes tokens for sensitive data with the mapping kept in a token vault.

The figure's example outputs: Base64 of '4111 1111 1111 1111' starts with NDExMSAxMTEx and decodes without a key; a Fernet token starts with gAAAAAB and a wrong key raises InvalidToken; a random 'tok_' token returns the data through a dictionary acting as the vault.
claims.verified_by: No external page describes this exact output; observed by executing the code on the authoring machine. Used the Python standard library (base64, secrets) and cryptography 50.0.1 (Fernet); the PyPI page identifies the package only.

claims.claim_vi: In public-key (asymmetric) encryption the public key can be distributed because it can only encrypt; only the private key decrypts. Observed with RSA-OAEP: data encrypted using only the public key was decrypted by the private key, and the public key object has no decrypt operation.
claims.verified_by: No external page describes this exact output; observed by executing the code on the authoring machine. Executed RSA-OAEP with cryptography 50.0.1. The property is standard public-key cryptography; NIST's glossary entry for a public key, cited by a reviewer, was not reachable from the authoring environment.

claims.claim_vi: Symmetric encryption should use AES with a key of at least 128 bits (ideally 256); dedicated secret or key management systems add protection at the cost of complexity and administrative overhead.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of the OWASP repository.

claims.claim_vi: In almost all circumstances passwords should be hashed with modern adaptive algorithms rather than encrypted; hashing is a one-way function.
claims.verified_by: Read from a local clone of the OWASP repository.

claims.claim_vi: Anyone who obtains the token vault can recover the original data, so the security of vault-based tokenization concentrates in the vault.
claims.verified_by: Author's inference from the described design (mapping stored in a vault); not checked against a standard.

claims.claim_vi: Tokenization is often used for payment card data and helps with PCI DSS compliance.
claims.verified_by: Carried from the source as general description; not independently checked. The OWASP Cryptographic Storage cheat sheet does not mention tokenization.

design_notes_vi: Một dữ liệu mẫu cho cả ba cách để so sánh; thẻ cuối nói mỗi cách có một chỗ phải bảo vệ. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source calls tokenization 'highly secure' because tokens cannot be reverse-engineered; true for random vault-based tokens, but the risk moves to the token vault, which the lesson names as the place to protect.
Source does not distinguish hashing; the lesson adds a short note that hashing is a separate one-way operation.
